To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
migrant housing squats are an integral part of the ‘Corridors of Solidarity’ that are being built across Europe.
the self-organised housing of migrants in squats is an important form of social reproduction and political resistance against the violence and precarity of border regimes.
Migrants’ self-organisations are a form of commoning, in which autonomous socio-political networks of solidarity are created beyond and against the State and humanitarian provision.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: How do migrants’ self-organized responses to housing in Europe challenge the dominant modes of governance and the prevailing notions of citizenship?
the ways in which migrants’ self-organization in relation to housing challenges the state, its borders and its institutions

the following questions: How can we understand the politics of migrant housing squats in relation to institutional forms of accommodation? What are the political implications of the struggles emerging in migrant housing squats? How are these struggles rearticulating the meaning of citizenship?

migrant squats are an integral part of the ‘solidarity corridors’ that are being established throughout Europe, where grass-roots social movements engaged in antiracist, anarchist and anticapitalist politics coalesce with the migrants to devise noninstitutional responses to the border regime’s violence.

the article aims at understanding the ways in which migrant housing squats are being constituted as a space of inhabitance, beyond, against and with citizenship.
the squats are not only spaces of refuge and social reproduction, but also of political struggle.
The main takeaway from our work is that

migrants squats are not only a response to the lack of adequate housing provision, but are an integral part of the struggle to create alternative spaces of social reproduction, solidarity and political organisation.
the struggle against border regimes and the struggle for housing are intertwined.

migrants’ self-organization is an important aspect of the current European political conjuncture, which is characterized by an increasing securitization of migration, the rise of right-wing populism and a general decline in social welfare.
